instructions: Put the rice in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered.
Meanwhile, pull the small tough muscle off the side of each scallop. Pat them very dry with paper towels, then sprinkle them with 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper.
Mince the garlic. Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley and cut the lemon into wedges.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high for 2 minutes, until it's very hot. Add 1 tbsp of the oil, then half the scallops in a single layer with space between them.

Cook without moving them for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is deep golden and they let go of the pan. Flip them and cook for 1 minute. They're done when they're just opaque in the middle. Transfer them to a plate.
Wipe the pan, add 1 tbsp of the oil and cook the rest of the scallops the same way. Transfer them to the plate.
Take the pan off the heat. Add the remaining 3 tbsp oil, the garlic and two-thirds of the chopped parsley. Stir for 20 seconds, until the garlic smells fragrant and hasn't browned.
Return the scallops and any juices on the plate to the pan, then squeeze in the juice of 2 lemon wedges. Turn the scallops to coat them in the persillade.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Sprinkle the rest of the parsley over the top.
Serve with the rice and the remaining lemon wedges.
method_notes: Scallops seared hard and finished in a garlic and parsley persillade made in the same pan, which is what the sources for this dish share. The lead (Jardiner Malin) uses butter with the oil; butter is left out here to keep the dish dairy-free, so the persillade is all olive oil. The lead suggests tagliatelle, which isn't gluten-free, so plain rice goes with it, and the lemon comes from the other seared and grilled scallop pages. Only unrated pages were readable for the exact dish, so this is a fallback lead; there's a lot less sauce than a cream or wine version, which is the dish.
